name: Beata Szydło - § 6 - Am 5
title: REPORT on the security of energy supply in the EU
part_text: 6. Emphasises the importance of taking into account the different specificities of Member States and their regions, including Europe’s outermost territories, when adopting energy policies focused on renewables, particularly in areas with less favourable conditions for solar and wind power; underlines that for certain regions, a pragmatic and regionally sensitive approach is essential for prioritising security of supply and affordability of energy prices; recalls, in this context, the role of modern coal- and lignite-fired power plants, among other technologies, in ensuring energy security and avoiding premature, industry-disrupting measures, as well as securing a phased and realistic shift, enabling all regions to actively participate in and benefit from the development of a modern energy system; stresses the importance of finding a balance between the development of renewable energy sources and the preservation of the primary sector, in order to avoid the adverse effects of the deployment of certain renewable technologies;
